title: Masked builds are 1 to 5% slower since the scans became generic over KeyScheme
body:
Commit `023778c` made the count and gather scans generic over `KeyScheme`. Each scan calls `count_chunk` or `gather_chunk`, or on a CPU with BMI2 a copy of the same loop compiled with BMI2 (`count_chunk_bmi2`, `gather_chunk_bmi2`). `MaskedKeys::key` branches on its `bmi2` field and calls `masked_key_pext` or `masked_key`.

Masked builds came out 1 to 5% slower than `75d429b`, which had the separate `count_masked_pext` and `gather_masked_pext`. Jack accepted the cost for now, to revisit when looking for performance across all of sufr.

The benchmark suite on `bench` ran with 100 MiB fixtures, 4 threads and median of 5, on an AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D. The output of both builds matched.

| row | `75d429b` | `023778c` |
|---|---|---|
| `normal` | 1.35 s | 1.33 s |
| `protein` | 1.27 s | 1.26 s |
| `mask-dna` | 1.41 s | 1.47 s |
| `mask-dna-heavy` | 1.59 s | 1.67 s |
| `mask-dna-wide` | 1.97 s | 2.00 s |
| `mask-protein` | 1.63 s | 1.68 s |

Before the BMI2 copies of the loops were added, `MaskedKeys::key` called `masked_key_pext` out of line, and masked builds took 14 to 21% longer.

## Open

- What the remaining gap is. Nobody has compared the generated code. Candidates nobody has checked: the per-suffix branch on `self.bmi2` inside `key`, and the generic loop compiling differently from the old `count_masked` with a closure.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/16cf998c
notes.text: Commit `9f9c913` moved tie runs and boundary LCPs onto `KeyScheme`. Against `023778c` at 100 MiB, `mask-dna` went from 1.46 to 1.56 s, about 7%. The other mask rows moved by 2% or less. `MaskedKeys::order_ties` now sorts each tie run by descending position after the key sort, where `sort_masked_partition` sorted by key and position in one pass. Nobody has checked whether that change causes the 7%. Jack accepted the cost for now and plans a run on a whole genome, such as hg38, to see whether it holds at that size.
